purpose: Loratadine is used to relieve allergy symptoms like sneezing, runny nose, itchy or watery eyes, and itchy skin. It also helps with hives. It works all day long, so most people only need to take it once a day.
how_it_works: When your body encounters something you are allergic to, like pollen or pet dander, it releases a chemical called histamine, which causes your allergy symptoms. Loratadine blocks the spots in your body where histamine tries to attach, so it cannot cause those annoying symptoms. Unlike older antihistamines, loratadine is designed to not cross into your brain much, so it usually does not make you feel sleepy.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate loratadine very well. The most common side effects are headache, dry mouth, and feeling a little tired. Some people may experience an upset stomach or nervousness. Serious side effects are very rare.
warnings: Although loratadine rarely causes drowsiness, a small number of people may still feel a little sleepy, so be cautious the first time you take it before driving. Tell your doctor if you have severe liver or kidney problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Check with your doctor or pharmacist before taking it if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Also, check other medications you take for antihistamines to avoid doubling up.
typical_dosing: Adults and children 6 years and older: take one 10 mg tablet or 10 mg of liquid by mouth once a day. Children ages 2 to 5: the usual dose is 5 mg once a day. It can be taken with or without food. Do not take more than one dose in 24 hours.
